partners.mechanism_chain: CD79A (HGNC:1770) —DISRUPTS→ B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050732); CD79B (HGNC:1771) —DISRUPTS→ B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050732); B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050732) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:00114210); B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050732) —LEADS_TO→ Absent B cells (HP:0003240); B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050732) —LEADS_TO→ Agammaglobulinemia (HP:0004325). Mutations in CD79A (causing disease A, likely a form of immunodeficiency related to B cell development) and CD79B (causing agammaglobulinemia 3) both disrupt the B cell receptor signaling pathway. This disruption leads to impaired B cell maturation and function, resulting in phenotypes such as recurrent infections, absent B cells, and agammaglobulinemia.

partners.mechanism_chain: CD79B (HGNC:2180) —DISRUPTS→ B cell receptor signaling pathway (WP:WP466); B cell receptor signaling pathway (WP:WP466) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent infections (HP:0002664); IL6R (HGNC:5554) —DISRUPTS→ IL-6 signaling pathway (WP:WP103); IL-6 signaling pathway (WP:WP103) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent infections (HP:0002664).
